title: DOS, Amiga and ST remakes and application sources
summary: Add sixteen qualified game and application-source projects after reviewing 28 roots; record twelve deferrals and derivative cases.
notes: Root personally searched all six requested platform families and reviewed 28 pinned roots. Sixteen qualified game/reconstruction/application entries and twelve deferrals or duplicate-adjacent cases. No discovery worker used. Separate original-author remakes, source preservation, subsystem research and unfinished engines; do not infer fidelity from screenshots or a README claim. No upstream software executed. Pinned bytes are ephemeral local review material only; retained submission carries immutable proof identities without source excerpts.

sources.reason: Compact 16-bit assembly remake of PC-DOS DONKEY, with explicit DOS COM versus boot-sector build switch and BIOS/CGA display routines. Concrete native remake source rather than a screenshot-only project.

JavaScript port with documented MZ4 14-by-18 column-major level records, tile-behavior bits and SYM 24-by-32 sprite format. C viewers and gameplay source expose actual format work. An unknown level-header span remains explicitly unidentified.

VB6 remake of Lemmings and Oh No More Lemmings, with dedicated lemming simulation, level loader/rendering, level editing, music and timing modules. Original data/behavior resemblance is not proof of binary equivalence.

Separates DOS graphics/world-data import, semantic simulation and software UI from a Bevy shell. Original-file import drives classic mode; enhanced artwork and explicit original-bug repairs change presentation/behavior. Does not claim matching original machine code.

Concrete LS11/R3, sprite/palette, portrait and scenario-VM analysis with Godot implementation. Handoff is ahead of root README: opening/dialogue and battle-map viewing exist, but map-chip mapping is guessed and battle rules, numbers, AI, music playback, saves and politics remain open.

AutoHotkey-H source reconstructs Logical ball movement, rotator challenges, timers, win/loss states and INI-defined levels. Threaded drawing/music and game code are present despite the minimal README.

C# engine recreates spinners, teleporters, color modifiers, directional blocks and level-set handling for Logical. README fidelity claim is qualified as a remake intent, not a verified original-game comparison.

Original programmer reconstructs the 1992 German AMOS parser adventure as DOM-free state/rule logic with inventory, per-room flags, English/German UI and 13 locations. Progress-blocking bugs are deliberately fixed.

Unity remake includes original levels and basic interaction, but author explicitly says robot programming is missing, which prevents some levels being solved. Important partial engine rather than a completed game.

Bootloader and CP/M BIOS use TOS BIOS/XBIOS, with BDOS trap-vector preservation, disk-cache changes and adapted programs. BIOS source records newer TPA changes than the README; do not assume its fixed-address description is current.
Preserves Allan Pratt Atari TOS RCS 5 port and a m68k-atari-mint rebuild intended to lift the old command-line limit. Author warns rebuilt programs are larger/slower; original DIFF remains unchanged.

Rewrites the Spanish Dictator simulation through SBASIC and Odin into Nim, with decisions, audiences, assassination, month and news modules. This is deliberate translation/reimplementation with improvements, not original Sinclair BASIC recovery.
Single substantial DIV program defines the board, movement, enemy and scoring structure with game assets. Original behavior coverage and exact timing are not independently established.

Java/Slick2D remake of DOS Vlak with game/editor/options states, component-based entities and level management. Current changelog adds Java 21 support while an internal version constant still says 0.8.

Author explicitly calls this a LionEngine prototype/use case; original assets and title do not establish full Tyrian gameplay recovery. Existing OpenTyrian-style source work is a different provenance.
Gameplay README describes multiplayer arena powerups without establishing which original DOS data or behavior is restored. Defer until original-game relationship is evidenced beyond search metadata.

Useful Star Trek Borg engine remake, but the documented original is Windows 95 media rather than a requested DOS/Amiga/ST/CPC/C64/Spectrum target. Keep adjacent lead, not a rejection of source quality.
Puzzle remake source exists, but reviewed build notes do not establish original DOS-game provenance. Needs original-title/engine relationship review before promoting as restoration.
Andrew Jenner Digger Remastered Unix derivative. Existing RikusW/digger-unix already represents this recovery lineage; no independently distinct reconstruction established for another entry.

Inspected raylib Python program primarily builds a track/grid interaction prototype. Full original train scheduling, routing and economy recovery is not established; defer rather than treat rebuilt branding as completion.
Small Unity player/asteroid scripts without documented original data formats or recovered game behavior. Defer generic clone/prototype until source provenance is clear.
Tree contains an empty assets/galcon.js and framework/static material. No substantive reconstructed game implementation established.

Python remake and exploratory FIN decoder exist, but decoder is an interactive byte dump with explicit early exit and unresolved compression. No established original data/engine reconstruction sufficient for promotion this pass.
Current tree has README, license and screenshots only. No LibGDX game implementation source is published despite the remake description.

source_updates.reason: Third remake by Mario Latzig includes original normal/tutorial/demo towers, robot programming and a tower editor. ADF-versus-2009 conversion cross-check identifies real losses in old titles, timing and tiles, rather than assuming the older remake authoritative.

Recreates board pieces, closed-loop detection/removal, scoring and timed placement in HTML/CSS/SVG/JavaScript. Only the endless mode is implemented; original has three modes. Graphics are intentionally simplified from the original palette.
README explicitly identifies this as distribution/marketing repository; game source is maintained separately. Preserve playable-port lead without calling this public engine source.
3D models, rendering assets and prototype material, without established original CPC logic/data recovery. Retain adjacent remake lead rather than claim a faithful reconstruction.
